newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Coal & Allied lifts pay offer to strikers.
newsitem.headline: Coal & Allied lifts pay offer to strikers.

text.p: Coal and Allied Industries Ltd said it had raised the average pay rise on offer to striking miners at its New South Wales Hunter Valley No.1 mine to A$170 a week from A$150 a week.
"Hunter Valley No.1 mine management today increased the pay and benefits in the collective agreement on offer to striking workers," it said.
Coal and Allied also said it has offered a voluntary redundancy package of A$46,000 to any employee who does not want to go back to work.
The collective agreement would give the lowest paid employee at the mine A$74,000 a year and the highest paid over A$87,000 a year based on a 42.5 hour work week, Coal and Allied said.
The five-week old strike centres the company's bid to offer individual workplace agreements to all staff at the mine,
Coal and Allied is 71 percent owned by Anglo-Australian mining house Rio Tinto Ltd.
Coal and Allied has estimated each day of the strike is costing the company about A$1 million in lost revenue.
Coal and Allied also said it has increased non-cash benefits to employees, as well.
Under the collective agreement, workers would receive improved superannuation and medical benefits it valued at A$3,000 per employee per year.
"The cost of the pay rises and redundancies will be offset by dramatically improved productivity, which will flow from the elimination of outdated work practises," the company said.
